In a mental exercise, I should ask things of myself.

1. **Are you a good person?** Not really. I'm not bad, evil, or malicious. But I am dishonest and lazy. [Looking at the seven sins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_deadly_sins), I will say that I rarely fall privy to gluttony, pride, and avarice. I sometimes fall to wrath, but only the feelings; I don't remember taking actions out of anger within the last year. I sometimes fall to envy as well. My worst sins are of lust and of sloth, the latter being the most damaging. So, I do have some work to do to be able to call myself "good".

2. **How can you manage envy?** By understanding that everyone has pluses and minuses. I am just paying attention to their pluses. They also have troubles. They are just different from mine. Since they are so different, comparisons are futile. My only fair competitor is myself. Stop looking outside so much and focus on how you can maximize your own situation.

3. **How can you manage lust?** For some reason, I feel like this one should be excusable... I can't really stop it. The way I am managing it right now should suffice. In the mind of some, it is not right, but it doesn't hurt anyone, so it should be fine.

4. **How can you manage sloth?** Ugh.

A question that I was troubled by in the past came again at my doorstep today, bringing a small pint of tears with it as well. "Why am I not good enough? What about me is inadequate? What is wrong with me?" I thought it would trouble me all day, but I used up the pint and feel okay. Sometimes I ask, "Why me?", but it seems like there's no one to answer this or any other existential question. My self-worth has been under question, but now the cause for question has mostly shifted to other things.

Emptiness still echoes in my chest. It will remain for some years, it seems. I fear it will be forcibly filled then. The emptiness rang louder today, which prompted questions. I know what's wrong with me. It's my color, my tainted/different features, my illness. It's my naivete and hope and perseverance. It's my nature to catch like velcro, even to what doesn't match.

It's fine, really. That I learned my lesson, it's a good thing. To learn about how deep and wide the abyss is between reality and ideality. To learn that burdens are burdens no matter where, that everything comes at a price, that pieces that don't match cannot go together. Sometimes you get too caught up in a dream, foolishly tangled, and you have to learn the hard way. You have to trip over reality, fall hard, bleed, and cry like a baby. Then you look back and see hindsight is 20/20 and that dreams are stupid so stop dreaming because the definition of adulthood is the death of dreaming. Well, it looks like I haven't quite finished the pint yet. Almost done.
